ai.description: This small frog reaches 25–30 mm. It is brown with a distinct, light-colored vertebral stripe and dark dorsal markings. Key features include a pointed snout and a granular, tuberculate skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Minervarya mysorensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous glandular fold running along the sides of its back, unlike similar *Minervarya* species.
ai.habitat: *Minervarya mysorensis* inhabits moist deciduous forests and grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found near water bodies at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mysore frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects near water bodies and damp ground within its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Minervarya mysorensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of approximately 200–300 eggs in small, shallow water bodies.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Minervarya mysorensis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at moderate to high elevations.
ai.callDescription: The Mysore Frog emits a series of short, high-pitched "tink-tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation near stagnant water bodies or paddy fields during the monsoon.
